It leaves room for the student to respond differently in another context. It also avoids turning an adult's interpretation into an unquestionable statement of the student's wishes. Include how much support was provided and who observed the response. If adults disagree about what a response means, name the uncertainty and ask what information or professional input would help. Avoid treating limited speech as evidence that the person has no preferences or nothing to contribute. Participation might include joining a portion of a discussion or sharing an appropriately supported contribution prepared in advance. Do not assume those possibilities replace any requirement that applies to the particular meeting. Ask the Team how the student's perspective will be included and who will support access. On this one, I stayed at Disney’s Pop Century Resort—and the pool was right outside my room. An excellent detail. Possibly the detail I should lead with. I flew JetBlue to Florida for Fiber Connect with Graphical Networks. The conference took place at the beautiful Gaylord Palms Resort & Convention Center, while Pop Century was my home base. Around the work came a lovely Skyliner ride, the Crystal Palace buffet, and a little time at Disney. Michael and James stayed home. Gaylord Palms was a lovely setting for the conference. Staying at Pop Century gave the trip another atmosphere altogether: bright, playful, and unmistakably Disney. And then there was that pool.
